body_markdown:
The


[ARIA Awards](https://www.aria.com.au/awards/) turned 40 this year, and for the second year running, Spotify returned as presenting partner of Australia’s biggest night in music. Two years into our three-year partnership, we set out to build on the success of our debut and give fans everywhere even more ways to connect with the artists shaping Australian music.


“Forty years of the ARIA Awards is a milestone worth celebrating, and this year’s lineup reflected everything that makes Australian music special, from the icons who shaped our sound to the breakthrough artists defining what comes next,” said


**Mikaela Lancaster** , Spotify’s Managing Director for Australia & New Zealand. “Spotify was proud to partner with ARIA on this landmark night and help bring Australian music to fans here at home and around the world.”


## **A record-breaking year for fans**


For the first time in ARIA history, more than 1 million fan votes were cast across Spotify and the ARIA website, setting a new record. Fans voted in four categories: Song of the Year, Best Australian Live Act, Best Video, and Most Popular International Artist.


A dedicated ARIA hub on Spotify gave listeners a place to discover this year’s nominees, explore their music, and support their favorites. Beyond the app, a campaign spanning more than 800 billboards and screens brought Australian artists to audiences at home and abroad.


## **Tame Impala’s global moment**


The second-ever ARIA Global Impact Award presented by Spotify went to


[Tame Impala](https://open.spotify.com/artist/5INjqkS1o8h1imAzPqGZBb) , recognizing


**Kevin Parker** , the musician behind the project, for an extraordinary year on the world stage.


Following the release of his fifth album,


[Deadbeat](https://open.spotify.com/album/5WulAOx9ilWy1h8UGZ1gkI) , Tame Impala racked up nearly 4.5 billion global streams over the past 12 months. Nearly 98 million listeners discovered his music, and fans added it to their playlists more than 141 million times. Global hit “


[Dracula](https://open.spotify.com/track/1NXbNEAcPvY5G1xvfN57aA?si=5dea98b3cb4c40b6) ” became the biggest hit of Parker’s career, spending 18 weeks in the ARIA Top 10, reaching No. 1 on US Alternative Radio, and earning Gold or higher in 16 countries. His biggest markets include the U.S., U.K., Mexico, and Brazil.


“Being this year’s recipient of the Global Impact Award at the ARIAs is huge. It’s such an honor, obviously,” said Parker, who accepted the award from Australian music icon


[Darren Hayes](https://open.spotify.com/artist/0ihJnGEjNnbM6uuTn3RHMo) . “I’m so proud to be an Aussie artist, always.”


## **Setting the stage at Machine Hall**


ARIA Week kicked off on November 16 with the second Spotify Artist Party at Sydney’s Machine Hall. ARIA nominee


[Yes Boone](https://open.spotify.com/artist/38AjHGnP1jV6bCn2fnx4F5) set the tone with a DJ set as guests arrived. Headliner


[Genesis Owusu](https://open.spotify.com/artist/1HvH97rzvCH6lfnLlgyfke) —who co-led this year’s ARIA nominations with eight—then delivered a pulsating set built on


[Normal Pleasure](https://open.spotify.com/artist/4khBCYLWyHyGoOpkAoJkyI) ’s remixes of his album, first created for Spotify’s Turn Up Aus event in July. In another one of the night’s standout moments,


[Larissa Lambert](https://open.spotify.com/artist/1tM4ox3QsSpl3R2VwLjJ47) performed “So Close” from the mezzanine, singing out to the crowd below.


[2charm](https://open.spotify.com/artist/7HKUxdZeGZQHLE7vFG4Syr) closed out the night, DJing the after-party.

## **One big night for Australian music**


On November 18, the celebration moved to Sydney’s Hordern Pavilion for the 40th ARIA Awards, broadcast live across Australia and streamed to international audiences on YouTube. The evening included electrifying performances from Genesis Owusu,


[Ecca Vandal](https://open.spotify.com/artist/0NhKCHTPG7Sz62S3zxV1Cf) ,


[DMA’S](https://open.spotify.com/artist/1iUTUix5kea176M0uJTsh4) ,


[BOY SODA](https://open.spotify.com/artist/2gorlgsMUJH6TSfTPhaCdW) , and newly inducted Hall of Fame legends


[Spiderbait](https://open.spotify.com/artist/6P7kkhED6EPrfoZuxz20Fo) .

NEXT


Ecca Vandal took home the Michael Gudinski Breakthrough Artist Award presented by Spotify. The singer-songwriter,


[one of Spotify’s Artists to Watch 2026](https://newsroom.spotify.com/2026-01-12/artists-to-watch-2026/) in rock/alternative, has also been supported across editorial playlists like


[New Music Friday AU & NZ](https://open.spotify.com/playlist/37i9dQZF1DWT2SPAYawYcO) ,


[the new alt](https://open.spotify.com/playlist/37i9dQZF1DX82GYcclJ3Ug) , and


[Local Noise](https://open.spotify.com/playlist/37i9dQZF1DWVHkDVXyDP0L) .


Tame Impala won Album of the Year for


*Deadbeat* , leading the night with seven awards, including Best Solo Artist, Best Pop Release, and the fan-voted Song of the Year for “Dracula.”


Other notable wins included


[G Flip](https://open.spotify.com/artist/4SdIXLzfabqU61iK7SnKAU) , who took home the fan-voted awards for Best Australian Live Act and Best Video for “


[Bed on Fire](https://open.spotify.com/track/01IJ2feBkPtQgQi68nx9nl?si=87889659661b46b2) ,” and DMA’S, who won Best Group and Best Rock Album.


“Congratulations to all of this year’s nominees and winners, and to ARIA for an unforgettable celebration of four decades of local music,” Spotify’s Mikaela Lancaster said. “Australian music has never traveled further or faster, and Spotify will keep doing our part to help these artists be heard everywhere.”


*See the full list of winners on the*[ARIA Awards site](https://www.aria.com.au/awards/) *, then stream Spotify’s Best of ARIA Awards playlist to celebrate Australian music at its finest.*
